samples.summary: No test covers an edit/delete of an existing thread with an unknown commentId (the 404 guard in `assertCommentAuthor`)
samples.evidence: The new parameterized suite's 404 test (`'404s an edit or a delete of a thread that does not exist'`, spec line 679) only passes a bad *threadId* ('nope'), which is caught by `mutateMap`'s `findThread` check (comments.controller.ts:575) before authorization ever runs. Nothing anywhere exercises a valid thread + unknown commentId, which is the only path through `assertCommentAuthor`'s `if (!comment) throw new NotFoundException('Comment not found')` (comments.controller.ts:528). Impact if that guard regressed: `editComment` would fall through to `applyEditComment` returning `undefined` and the route would answer 200 with `{ threadId, comment: undefined }` — a silent no-op edit reported as success. `applyEditComment`'s undefined return is unit-tested in comment-ops.spec.ts:189, but the controller's translation of it into a 404 is not.

samples.summary: The "nothing was written" assertion cannot distinguish authorize-before-update from authorize-inside-update; the fake `update` has no rollback
samples.evidence: The test comments at spec:630 and spec:483 claim "the check runs before the CRDT transaction opens", but `harness`'s fake document (spec:31-34) implements `update: (fn) => fn(root)` against the very same object `getRoot()` returns, with no transaction and no rollback. `expect(threadsOf(root).t1.comments).toHaveLength(2)` therefore holds identically if `authorize?.()` were moved inside `doc.update` ahead of `mutate` — the ordering the comment says is under test is not observable in this harness. The assertion is not vacuous (it would fail if authorization were skipped entirely), but it is weaker than its comment claims and the ordering property in `mutateMap` (comments.controller.ts:562, 578) has no covering test.

samples.summary: The flat-root edit response is never checked for JSON-serialisability, and the fixture's plain-number timestamps hide the bigint hazard the repo documents
samples.evidence: `flatRoot()` (spec:559-587) stores `createdAt: 5` as a plain number, unlike real Yorkie storage where `toYorkieMs` writes `bigint` Longs (comment-ops.ts:59). The sheet suite guards the serialisation hazard explicitly for replies (`expect(() => JSON.stringify(reply)).not.toThrow()`, spec:229) because a `bigint` in a response makes `res.json()` throw a 500, but neither the new doc/pdf edit test nor the existing sheet edit test applies that check to the `editComment` response — they only assert `typeof editedAt === 'number'` (spec:610). A bigint leaking through any other field of `{ threadId, comment }` (e.g. `createdAt` if `copyComment` regressed) would pass these tests while 500ing in production.

samples.summary: The `doc` and `pdf` parameterizations exercise identical code, so the second run adds only a docKeyPrefix assertion
samples.evidence: `describe.each([['doc','doc-'],['pdf','pdf-']])` (spec:541) drives both types through the same flat-root branch of `mutateMap` (comments.controller.ts:572-584); the only type-dependent behavior is `prefixFor(type)`. The fixture's anchor differs (`pdf-region` vs `docs-range`, spec:564-567) but no edit/delete code path reads `anchor` at all, so eight of the nine assertions in each `pdf` run re-test bytes already covered by the `doc` run. Harmless duplication, worth knowing it is not the extra path coverage the block comment (spec:547-553) implies.

samples.summary: The documented "editing does not notify" behavior has no test
samples.evidence: comments.controller.ts:433-435 states editing deliberately emits no notification, and deletes likewise call `mutateMap` without `notify`. The notifications describe block (spec:691-840) covers thread/reply/resolve/reopen/self-mention/failure but never asserts `notificationService.createFromComment` is left uncalled by `editComment`, `deleteComment` or `deleteThread`. finding.summary: No test covers comment edit/delete (and its author-only authorization) on the flat-root document types (doc / pdf)
finding.evidence: `describe('ApiV1CommentsController on other document types')` (spec lines ~326-380) only exercises `list`, `reply` and `setResolved` on a `doc` root. The whole non-sheet branch of `mutateMap` (comments.controller.ts, the `withDocument<void, FlatCommentRoot>` path that calls `authorize?.(doc.getRoot().comments)` and then `mutate(root.comments)`) is never exercised for `deleteThread`, `deleteComment` or `editComment`. Every authorship test lives under `describe('edit / delete authorship')`, whose `seededThread()` uses `harness('sheet', sheetRoot())`. If the flat-root branch stopped calling `authorize` (or called it with the wrong map), the suite would stay green while any workspace member could delete or rewrite another user's comments on a word-processor document or a PDF — the exact guard the controller docblock says it added because the editor only enforces it client-side.

verdict.reason: The spec does cover edit/delete authorship on the flat-root (doc/pdf) branch. comments.controller.spec.ts:541-689 is a `describe.each([['doc','doc-'],['pdf','pdf-']])` suite titled 'ApiV1CommentsController edit / delete authorship on a %s' whose docblock explicitly targets the flat-root `mutateMap` branch and its `authorize?.(doc.getRoot().comments)` call. Against a `flatRoot()` fixture with c1 authored by user 7 and c2 by user 9, it asserts: editComment by a non-author rejects with ForbiddenException and leaves the stored body unchanged (spec:596-599); the author's edit succeeds, stamps editedAt, mutates the stored root, and uses the type's docKeyPrefix (spec:601-613); deleteComment by a non-author rejects with ForbiddenException with the comment count unchanged (spec:623-632); author delete of own reply succeeds (spec:634-644); deleting the opening comment collapses the thread (spec:646-653); deleteThread by a non-opener rejects with ForbiddenException with the thread still present (spec:655-663); the opener's delete succeeds and a repeat 404s (spec:665-677); and edit/delete of an absent thread 404s (spec:679-687). If the flat-root branch dropped or misdirected `authorize` (comments.controller.ts:572-584), the ForbiddenException expectations and the no-write assertions would fail. The finding's claim that all authorship tests use `harness('sheet', sheetRoot())` describes only the earlier sheet suite (spec:453-539), not this one.
